import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a total sales per product visualization
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sales_per_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()
sns.barplot(data=sales_per_product, x='product', y='total', palette='viridis')

# Customize the plot
plt.title('Total Sales per Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a total sales per product visualization
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sales_per_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()
sns.barplot(data=sales_per_product, x='product', y='total', palette='viridis')

# Customize the plot
plt.title('Total Sales per Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
